title: Tactile control elevation
summary: Give knobs, switches and buttons a consistent depth hierarchy by separating a control's face, edge, recess and pressed feedback.
when_to_use: The interface represents a physical instrument or benefits from explicit press depth.
avoid_when: The control is tiny, data-dense or primarily navigational.

anatomy.purpose: Defines hit area and semantic role.
Holds label or indicator and the base material.
Communicates the control's elevation relative to its panel.
Shows where the control meets the surrounding surface.

tokens.name: --amb-chamfer
tokens.purpose: Amount of edge break around the face.

tokens.name: --amb-fillet
tokens.purpose: Curvature of the transition to the panel.

states.name: idle
states.behavior: Raised face and edge share the scene's light direction.

states.name: active
states.behavior: Face appears to move inward; pressed state remains distinguishable without animation.

states.name: focus
states.behavior: Independent focus outline remains visible above material effects.

responsive: Keep the interactive hit target usable on touch screens even if the visual control is compact.
accessibility: Use a native control where possible.
Expose pressed state with aria-pressed only for toggle buttons; do not use it for momentary actions.
implementation_steps: Choose a small elevation scale shared by all tactile controls.
Create semantic structure before adding highlights and shadows.
Test pointer, keyboard and touch feedback with motion reduced.
